_about: Subjective view per upcoming match, keyed by ESPN match id, written by a scheduled task from recent news. Shown in each stat's 'Why' box and next to 'Our call'; never mixed into the numbers. Per stat (goals, corners, cards, shots, shots_on_target): {lean: higher|lower|same, call: short judgement call, text: reasoning}. Also: overall, sources (URLs), written_at (ISO). Never use 'lock', 'sure thing' or 'guaranteed'.

401883109.overall: Girona (4th) and Eibar (5th) are level on 24 points, so this is a direct fight for the play-off places; Girona won 2-1 at Oviedo last time out, while Eibar have gone five league games without a win despite creating plenty. Match-day checks found no new absences: Quique Álvarez has Vanat and Asprilla back from international duty but is short at the back, with Àlex Moreno banned and Furtado, Bryan Gil and Jastin García injured (all in the numbers), plus Javi Boñar (injured) and Holmes Junior (Spain Under-18), which the numbers don't know, so Abdul Mumin is expected at left-back. Jokin Aranbarri's Eibar miss only Gift, Imanol and Bernat and plan to stay compact and break quickly; Arbilla is one yellow from a ban. Alejandro Morilla of the Navarre committee referees, and his low card record is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already add for Àlex Moreno's absence from Girona's defence and take a little off for Bryan Gil and Jastin García. I still lean slightly higher, to about 2.3, because Girona are also without Boñar and Holmes Junior and are expected to use Mumin, a centre-back, at left-back against an Eibar side Quique Álvarez calls dangerous on the counter; no match-day news changed that.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, already lifted for Eibar conceding 44 corners in their last six. Aranbarri plans to sit compact and defend his box when Girona have the ball, which fits the home-heavy split the numbers already show (5.9 to 3.5), so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards and include referee Alejandro Morilla, who averages 4.9 cards a game against a 5.3 average, a cut of about 7%. The play-off stakes and Arbilla playing on four yellows point slightly up, Morilla's calm record slightly down, and both are close to what the numbers see, so I stay at 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots, already lifted for both sides' recent shooting (Eibar 91 in their last six). Girona's patched defence could give Eibar a little more, but Eibar will spend long spells defending deep while Girona's front line is close to full strength with Vanat back and Carles Pérez, Abel Ruiz and Pyshchur expected, so I stay at 28.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target and already count Eibar's accurate recent shooting (35 on target in six). With Girona missing Boñar and Holmes Junior on top of the counted ban, and a centre-back likely at left-back, Eibar's quick vertical attacks should find a little more, so I nudge it to about 9.4.

401883304.overall: Celta Fortuna (18th, 13 points, one win in ten) host Real Valladolid (14th, 18 points, six off the play-offs) at Balaídos in a match both sides need. Celta's reserve side play fast, open football but leak goals; centre-backs Joel López and Ribes are back from bans, Hugo Cuenca is now reported out after returning from Paraguay duty with discomfort, and Antañón is a doubt after travelling with the first team to the Bernabéu; Gavián, Somuah and Mateo Sobral are out (in the numbers). Valladolid, winners of their last two away games, miss Ojeda (banned) and Latasa (both in the numbers) plus right-back Trilli (not in the numbers), and Fran Escribá again stressed controlling the tempo against a young side. José Antonio Sánchez Villalobos referees and his high card record is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already boosting Valladolid for 14 goals in their last six and trimming them for Latasa and Ojeda. I lean slightly lower, to about 2.6, because Escribá wants a controlled game rather than an end-to-end one and Celta get two first-choice centre-backs, Joel López and Ribes, back from bans; Celta's leaky record (26 conceded) keeps the size small.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners and already add for Valladolid's recent corners (39 in six) against a Celta side that conceded 47. Trilli's absence takes away one of Valladolid's attacking full-backs, but Alejo is a like-for-like replacement, so nothing points either way and I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 7.9 cards and include referee José Antonio Sánchez Villalobos, who averages 6.2 cards a game against a 5.3 average (+21%), on top of Celta's heavy recent booking. A tense game between a side in the drop zone and one chasing the play-offs fits what the numbers already see, so I stay at 7.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots, already lifted for Valladolid's recent shooting (88 in six) and Celta's openness. Escribá's caution points slightly down and Celta's young, fast side slightly up, while Cuenca's absence and Antañón's doubt are too small to move it, so I stay at 27.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, boosted for Valladolid's 39 on target in their last six. Without Latasa (counted) Escribá has to find another option up front, and Celta keep their main scorer Álvaro Marín, so nothing new points either way and I stay at 9.8.

401882801.overall: Osasuna (16th, 12 pts, one win in their last five) host bottom side Málaga (20th, 5 pts, still without a league win since promotion) at El Sadar, a relegation game both need; Arrasate's Osasuna drew 1-1 with Athletic last time and Málaga lost 1-2 at home to Racing with ten men. Osasuna's 23-man list leaves out goalkeeper Aitor Fernández, Bretones and Rockson (all in the numbers) and includes Herrando, Aimar Oroz, Del Castillo and Diego Rico, who is back after individual training and may start at left-back, with Budimir leading the line. Málaga miss the banned Aznou and the injured Rafita (in the numbers), plus centre-back Calero, which the numbers don't know (reports say a muscle overload), and the long-term absentees Lobete and Ochoa, who have been out since the summer so their absence is already in the team's recent figures; Diego Murillo is back in the squad after his knee injury. Ricardo De Burgos referees, and the numbers already take cards off for his quiet record.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already give Málaga a small boost for Bretones being out. Málaga's back line is thinner than the numbers know: Aznou is banned and centre-back Calero is out of the squad, while Oroz is back to feed Budimir; Murillo's return softens that, so a small rise, about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, with both sides' recent corner counts already counted. Osasuna cross a lot from Rubén García and Raúl Moro for Budimir, and Rico's return adds another left-sided crosser, while Málaga, without a win, must come forward; nothing new points clearly either way, so I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards; they add Osasuna's recent cards (19 in six), take some off Málaga's quieter run and take 9% off for referee Ricardo De Burgos (3.6 a game in seven). They make no adjustment for the stakes, and a 16th-versus-20th relegation game with a winless side forced to take risks tends to be scrappy, so a small lean up, to about 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots and already add a lot for both sides' recent shooting and how much each concedes (about +11% each). Oroz's return and a patched-up Málaga defence point a little higher, but a nervy relegation game can slow things down, so I stay at 30.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, with Málaga's recent accuracy (33 on target in six) already counted. Budimir is fit and Málaga will field a reshuffled defence without Aznou and Calero, but I already give that a little through goals, so I stay at 9.6.

401874989.overall: Milan (5th, 24 points, four wins in five) host Frosinone (7th, 20 points), whose attack has been one of the league's busiest even though they lost 1-0 at Cagliari before the break. Frosinone under Alvini miss top scorer Raimondo (injured) and the suspended Bracaglia, both counted by the numbers; Birligea leads the line with Ghedjemis, Schmidt and Kvernadze behind him and Terzic at left-back. For Milan, Tomori is ruled out with a hamstring injury (not on the numbers' list, back for Cagliari) along with Gabbia, Loftus-Cheek, Chukwueze and Saelemaekers, and Pavlovic is still being judged day by day after his kidney problem, so the expected back four is Gila, De Winter, Diawara and Bartesaghi; Maignan is fit after his scare with France and Pulisic, back from the US only on Friday, is listed to start behind Gonçalo Ramos. Referee Luca Pairetto (4.9 cards a game) is already in the numbers; no official lineups were out when this was refreshed an hour before kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already cut a lot for Raimondo's absence (-19% on Frosinone's goals) and raised a little for both sides' recent form. Tomori, not on the numbers' list, is out and Pavlovic is short of fitness, so Diawara is expected beside De Winter in a makeshift back line against a fast, direct Frosinone side; Pulisic, back late from the US, is still expected to start, so I keep the mild nudge to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners and already raise Frosinone's side for their big recent corner count (+9%) while trimming Milan's (-4%). Frosinone's wingers Ghedjemis and Kvernadze drive that count and Milan have won few corners lately, both already in the figure, and the match-day news changes nothing in the wide areas, so I stay at about 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards and already add Pairetto's strict record (+35%; 4.9 a game over 31 games). It is not a rivalry and no new suspension risk was reported; Frosinone's quick wingers may draw fouls from a reshuffled Milan defence, but not enough to move a figure that already carries a strict referee, so I stay at about 5.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.3 shots, already lifted heavily for Frosinone's shooting (+24%) and cut for Milan's low recent volume (-6%). Milan's expected attack around Ramos, Pulisic and Moreira is their usual one, and Birligea has been Frosinone's starter for weeks, so the shooting volume should look like recent games; about 33.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, already raised for Frosinone's sharp recent form (+21%). With Tomori out (not counted) and Pavlovic not fully fit, Diawara is expected to start in a reshaped back line, which should give Frosinone's runners cleaner looks; a small nudge to about 11.1.

401875001.overall: Atalanta (12th, 14 points, two wins in their last nine league games) host Inter (3rd, 28 points, four wins in five) on Sunday night; Sarri's side won 1-0 at Monza last time but concede too often when opponents overload the flanks, and they also have Conference League games to manage. Atalanta's back line is the big story the numbers can't see: through the week Hien and Kossounou were still in the gym and on individual work and Kristensen was being judged day by day, so Scalvini and Kolasinac are expected in the middle, with Krstovic preferred to Scamacca up front and Raspadori possibly back on the bench (one report). Inter, under Chivu, are expected to start Thuram and Pio Esposito with Lautaro, back in group training after six weeks out, likely only from the bench; Akanji and Zielinski are fit, while Bonny (counted by the numbers) and Stankovic are out. Referee Fabio Maresca (4.8 cards a game) and a lively head-to-head are already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, already trimming Atalanta a little for recent form and the head-to-head and Inter for Bonny's absence. Atalanta are likely without Hien and Kossounou and possibly Kristensen, which the numbers don't know, and Inter's Thuram-Esposito pair with Lautaro to come on should find room against a stand-in back line; no late news changed that, so a mild lean up to about 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, already raised for Inter's recent corner count against an Atalanta side that has conceded many. Atalanta's 4-2-3-1 with overlapping full-backs and Inter's wing-backs are their usual way of playing, and a stand-in Atalanta defence is more likely to concede chances than extra corners, so nothing new points either way; about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and already add Maresca's high rate (+27%, 4.8 a game) and a lively head-to-head (+13%). No suspension threat, feud or change of referee has been reported this week, so I stay at about 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, already lifted 10% for Inter's recent shooting. Atalanta's makeshift centre-backs point up for Inter, but Chivu plans to share minutes between Thuram and Lautaro in a busy month and Lautaro only comes off the bench, so the two roughly cancel; about 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. With Scalvini and Kolasinac expected in the middle and Hien, Kossounou and possibly Kristensen missing, which the numbers don't know, Inter's forwards should get cleaner looks than the numbers assume; a small nudge to about 9.6.

401876400.overall: Marseille (5th-6th, 18 points, the league's top scorers with 22) have won five league games in a row under Bruno Genesio, the last 2-1 at Lens, while promoted Le Mans (16th, 8 points) have one league win all season and no clean sheet, though they drew 1-1 with Monaco before the break. Marseille miss only Emerson and Cornelius, both counted; Sports Mole reports Hojbjerg, Aguerd and Kondogbia came back from the international break without problems (this morning one report had Hojbjerg ill), and the expected side is unchanged with Gouiri (seven goals) up front. Le Mans miss Bourabaa (their main creator, counted), Sidibe and Rossignol, and two match previews now list captain and centre-back Samuel Yohou as doubtful with a head injury, which the numbers do not know. Marseille play Levski Sofia in the Europa League on Thursday but nothing points to rotation, and referee Eric Wattellier (3.5 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals: Marseille's run of form adds a little, and Bourabaa's absence already takes a big share (about -19%) off Le Mans' goals. New since this morning: two previews list Le Mans captain Yohou, the organiser of their back three, as doubtful with a head injury, which the numbers do not count, and Le Mans have yet to keep a clean sheet; as he is doubtful rather than ruled out, I nudge up only slightly, to about 3.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.0 corners, already trimmed for Le Mans winning few corners lately. Le Mans' back five with wing-backs Buades and Calodat and Marseille's narrow attacking trio cutting inside fit that picture, so I stay at 8.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and already take about 11% off for Eric Wattellier, who averages 3.5 cards a game. Le Mans have picked up more cards than expected lately, which is also counted; there is no rivalry or special stakes here, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots. Marseille are at near full strength and Genesio expects to dominate the ball, while Le Mans plan to sit in a block and break with two forwards; that is the picture the numbers already have and no rotation is reported, so I stay at 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target, already slightly lower for Marseille's recent accuracy. Gouiri has scored in each of his last three league games and Le Mans have no clean sheet this season, and a Le Mans defence possibly without Yohou could concede more clear chances, but the numbers see the form trends and his absence is not confirmed, so I stay at 9.4.

401882803.overall: Getafe (15th, 12 pts, joint-lowest scorers in the league with eight goals) host Atlético Madrid (3rd, 28 pts) on Sunday night; Atlético lost to Bayern and Barcelona before the break, their forwards Julián Álvarez, Sørloth and Jonathan David have only five league goals between them, and they host Viking in the Champions League on Wednesday. Getafe miss the banned Gudelj and the injured Uche and Juanmi (all in the numbers); Bordalás has Zaid Romero fit again, ruled out rotation and is expected to pair Satriano with Enes Ünal. Simeone confirmed Cuti Romero misses another game and Pubill (ankle) and Lookman are out (the latter two in the numbers); Le Normand is expected back beside Hancko, Arnau Ortiz may come in, and Baena, Giuliano Simeone and Julián Álvarez are question marks to start after long international trips. Jesús Gil Manzano referees and the numbers already add about 15% to cards for his record.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take Lookman, Pubill and the banned Gudelj into account. Getafe have scored only eight league goals in 12 games and worked on defence over the break with Zaid Romero back, while Atlético's strikers are misfiring and Simeone may hold some starters back after international travel and before Viking; a small trim to about 2.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners and already count Getafe's high recent corner count (38 in six). Getafe play direct and win corners from long balls and crosses, while Atlético lose some width without Lookman, which the numbers count; nothing new points either way, so 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards, including about 15% for referee Gil Manzano (5.2 cards a game) on top of both sides' card form. A Madrid-area game against a Bordalás side built on duels is usually heated, but with a strict referee already counted the number reflects that heat, so I stay at 6.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.6 shots, and recent form has already pushed both sides up (+14% Getafe, +8% Atlético). Getafe rely on long balls and stoppages, Gil Manzano's games tend to be stop-start, and Simeone usually controls a game like this away before a Champions League night, possibly with some starters rested; a small trim to about 24.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.4 shots on target. Getafe have struggled to create all season and worked on their defence over the break, while Atlético's forwards are short of form and Lookman's absence is already counted; a slight trim to about 7.25.

401883111.overall: Burgos (6th, 24 points, strong at home with 17 of 24 points) host Albacete (19th on 13 points, but five straight wins in league and cup under Joseba Etxeberria) after losing 3-1 at Leganés. Burgos are without forwards Jon Karrikaburu and David González and left-back Brais Martínez (nasal fracture surgery), confirmed again on match day; the numbers only take off González. Albacete get Munir back, but Puertas, San Bartolomé, Gámez, Obeng, Javi Moreno and Marín are listed injured; the numbers have Corpas suspended, while one preview lists him available after his ban, so his status is unclear. Sergio Francisco wants his side switched on from the start after conceding early lately, and Marta Huerta de Aza referees, with her below-average card record already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take off David González (about -11% on Burgos' goals). I lean lower, to about 2.0, because Karrikaburu, Burgos' other main scorer, is confirmed out again and the numbers don't know it, and Albacete are short of several attackers; Albacete's scoring run is already in the momentum figures.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, already adding for Burgos' 37 corners in their last six. Burgos will push Albacete back at El Plantío while Albacete, more direct under Etxeberria, have won plenty of corners lately (41 in six); all of that is in the numbers, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards: raised for both sides' recent bookings but cut about 9% for referee Marta Huerta de Aza, who shows 4.9 cards a game against a 5.3 average. Dadie, Vencedor, Galdames and Álex Rubio are one yellow from a ban, which can make them a little more careful, and the intense game Francisco expects is close to what the momentum figures count, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots, boosted strongly (+23%) for Burgos' 98 shots in their last six. With Karrikaburu and González both out, Burgos lose two of their main shooters and are expected to start Curro and Forés up front, so I trim slightly to about 25.5; Albacete's form with Munir back keeps it from falling further.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Without Karrikaburu as well as González, Burgos' finishing is thinner than the numbers assume, and Etxeberria says Albacete must be more clinical after wasting chances, so I go a little lower, to about 7.7.

401883110.overall: Bottom against top at the Alfonso Murube on Monday night (20:30 Spanish time): Ceuta are last with 5 points from 14 games (10 scored, 32 conceded) and have lost five in a row, while Almería have 32 points, 26 scored and 11 conceded, and are twelve games unbeaten in league and cup; Castellón's weekend win means they need to win here to go back top. Sergio Lobera, in his first full week and first home game in charge after a 2-0 loss at Tenerife, calls it a chance for a turning point, wants the Murube full (season-ticket holders get free tickets) and mentioned absences without naming anyone. Almería's squad list confirms captain Jorge Pulido is a late absence with an ankle problem, alongside Rodrigo Ely and Nico Melamed; only Melamed is in the numbers (about -6% on their goals), while Marcos Luna, Stefan Dzodic (back from a ban) and Brian Cipenga (back from international duty) return. Referee Eder Mallo Fernández, confirmed with Rubén Ávalos on VAR, gives about 5.5 cards a game, near the league average, and that record is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, already taking about 6% off Almería for Melamed and adding a little to Ceuta from last season's 3-2 home win in this fixture. What they don't see is now confirmed: Almería lose centre-back and captain Pulido late (Ely is also out), which should help Ceuta's thin attack led by Jordi Escobar, while Almería get Dzodic and Cipenga back and must win to retake top spot. Both sides point slightly up, so a mild +3%, about 3.3 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, 6.1 of them Ceuta's, already including their recent run of 44 corners in six games (+11% momentum). García Pimienta expects Ceuta to want the ball at home, which fits Lobera's possession style with high full-backs, and Almería with Cipenga back have more width on the break; none of this changes the corner count beyond what the numbers already see, so 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards, already counting Ceuta's heavy recent booking (+12% momentum) and referee Eder Mallo Fernández, whose 5.5 cards a game is close to the league average (+2.5%). A desperate home side in front of a full ground may foul to stop Almería's counters, but that is the pattern the numbers already see and there is no derby or other edge here, so I stay at 6.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.5 shots, with Ceuta's recent volume adding about 31% to their side and Almería's quieter attacking run taking about 7% off theirs. Lobera wants balance rather than all-out attack, and Almería without Pulido may concede a few more efforts but need few chances themselves; that sits within what the numbers already give, so 31.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. Ceuta hit the target only twice at Tenerife despite most of the ball and Lobera admits they score too little, which argues lower, but a reshuffled Almería back line without Pulido and Ely should make clean shots a little easier for them; those offset, so I stay at 10.3.

401875009.overall: Two struggling sides meet on Monday night: Monza are 18th with 7 points after four straight defeats, and Paolo Vanoli's Fiorentina are 15th with 9 points, unbeaten in three and scoring in ten straight games. Ivan Juric is banned and watches from the stands, so assistant Matteo Paro leads Monza; Juric asked for 'rage' against Fiorentina, and local press frame the game as one that could decide his future. Captain Pessina is back in the squad after three months out but will probably start on the bench, while Folorunsho (counted), Maye and Ngonge are out; Varela (9 goals in 10 games) leads the line. Fiorentina have Atta back in the squad for gradual minutes, Ndour recovered and Njie a late doubt with a thigh problem (Gnonto ready to start), with Pongracic and Parisi (both counted) out. Referee Daniele Doveri is one of Serie A's most lenient (2.7 cards a game), which the numbers already count.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already adding a little for both sides' recent scoring and leaky defending and taking about 4% off Fiorentina for Pongracic. Monza miss Ngonge and Maye, who are not in the numbers' list, but they have been out for weeks so recent form already reflects it, and top scorer Varela starts; Fiorentina have scored in ten straight games and get Atta and Ndour back. Nothing moves the total, so about 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners, already nudging up for Fiorentina's recent corner count (32 in six). Monza's 3-4-2-1 with Birindelli and Mangas as wing-backs and Fiorentina's 4-2-3-1 with Mastantuono and Njie or Gnonto wide are both sides' usual shapes, so I stay at about 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, already cut by about 29% for Doveri's lenient record, which I don't size again. This is a relegation scrap between sides two points apart, with Juric banned, his job reportedly on the line and him publicly asking his players for 'rage'; that tends to bring more fouls than a usual Doveri match, so a mild lean up to about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, already raised for both sides' recent shooting (+9% Monza, +14% Fiorentina). Monza need to attack at home and Fiorentina are close to full strength, but that is the picture the numbers already have, so about 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target, already lifted around 10% for each side's recent accuracy. Varela leads Monza's line with Mota and Robinson behind him, and Pellegrino leads Fiorentina's with Mastantuono and Gonçalves; nothing in the team news changes that, so about 10.

401879237.overall: Brentford (10th, 14 points, beaten 2-0 at Brighton before the break) host Everton (7th, 16 points, three straight wins in all competitions including 1-0 at Newcastle and a home win over Coventry) on Monday night, two points apart. Brentford are badly hit: Igor Thiago serves a ban after his red card at Brighton (the numbers count it, about -12.5% on their goals), Nathan Collins (knee) and Aaron Hickey (hamstring) are out for weeks, Rico Henry and Kaye Furo are sidelined, Dasilva and Milambo were only due a B-team run-out on Sunday, and Fabio Carvalho may make the squad; Callum Wilson is expected to lead the line. Everton report no new injuries, Moyes saying no one is ruled out, and are expected in their usual 4-2-3-1 with Thierno Barry (six league goals, the league's top xG) up front; Moyes becomes Everton's outright record holder for games managed tonight. Match-day checks found no change from this morning, and referee Craig Pawson (26 yellows and one red in six league games; 3.7 cards a game on record) is already counted, so the view stays as it was.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals, already taking about 12.5% off Brentford for Thiago's ban. They count missing players only by goals and assists, so they barely feel the loss of first-choice defenders Collins and Hickey, which helps Barry, the league's top chance-getter and strong in the air against a Brentford back line that relies on aerial duels. Wilson starting and Carvalho's possible return soften Brentford's attacking loss, so I keep it mild: about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners, already counting Brentford's low recent corner count (21 in six) and Everton's slightly higher one. Brentford still play wide and cross a lot, with a stand-in on the left for Hickey, and Everton line up in their usual 4-2-3-1, so nothing on match day points away from 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, already lowered about 10% for referee Craig Pawson's record and for calm past meetings. Everton have no suspensions and Moyes reports a fit squad, the table gap is two points and there is no rivalry between these clubs, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, already raising Everton for their recent volume (81 shots in six). Brentford lose Thiago's shooting but Wilson starts, while a weakened Brentford defence should let Everton's midfield trio of Armstrong, Garner and Dewsbury-Hall push on; the two roughly balance, so 27.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, already lowering Brentford for poor recent accuracy (19 on target in six). Losing Thiago's finishing is offset by Barry facing a back four without Collins and Hickey, so I stay at 8.2.

401882802.overall: A Monday-night Valencian relegation derby: Levante (18th, 11 points) host Elche (19th, 10 points), so the winner climbs past the other and possibly out of the drop zone. Luís Castro has the whole Levante squad available, with Manu Sánchez back from a hamstring injury and only Nakoha listed as a doubt. Martín Anselmi's Elche miss playmaker Marc Aguado (ankle), Adam Boayar and Yago, none of whom the numbers list (they only take off Ali Houary), while Villar, Sangaré and Lemar are back in training, Revivo was a midweek doubt and Cepeda returned late from Chile; Elche have lost their last two without scoring. Referee Francisco José Hernández Maeso (4.2 cards a game) is already counted, but the numbers do not flag the derby or the relegation stakes; no confirmed lineups yet at this refresh, so the view from this morning holds with the card lean trimmed slightly.
